title: Introduce RAG adaptive timebox playbook and lightweight tool-runner samples
author: Leah Murray
description:
Motivation: RAG workflows frequently need bounded tool execution (APIs, search calls, indexers) to avoid tail latency and to keep user-facing interactions responsive. This quickstart introduces an 'adaptive timebox' pattern: a canonical playbook and lightweight local tool-runner adapters (Node + Python) that demonstrate per-step timeouts, backoff policies, and graceful fallback behaviours.

What this PR adds (high level):
- A compact quickstart under quickstarts/adaptive-timebox that documents the pattern, trade-offs and recipe for instrumenting tool calls inside an agent-orchestrator flow.
- Two minimal example runners: a Node TypeScript runner that integrates with the RAG step payloads and a Python shim for teams wanting a quick serverless/local prototyping path. Both show a unified configuration for step timeouts and a small retry policy.
- A docs site page (docs/quickstarts/rag-adaptive-timebox.md) with step-by-step instructions, recommended defaults for production and a checklist for telemetry + chaos tests.
- A CI smoke job (ci/smoke-rag-quickstarts.yml) that runs the example runner end-to-end in CI with deterministic fixtures.
- Telemetry probes (telemetry/probes/timebox-probe.yaml) and tracing snippets to help validate SLOs during local runs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Quickstart content and examples implemented
- [x] Smoke CI added and passing on branch
- [x] Telemetry probe + docs included
- [x] Small unit + integration smoke tests
- [x] Reviewed and approved by eng + docs

Commits summary: Init scaffold with README and example stubs; Add node runner adapter and tooling; Add python runner shim; Docs: quickstart page + troubleshooting; CI: smoke job and fixtures; Tests: add deterministic fixture harness.

Testing notes: Run the Node runner locally: node examples/node-runner/start.js --fixture fixtures/sample-session.json. The runner supports a --timebox-ms override to exercise fallback behaviors. CI runs the same harness inside a container. The smoke CI is intentionally minimal to be fast (~90s).

Operational guidance: Default timebox recommendations are documented in the quickstart (100ms for non-critical enrichment calls, 300-500ms for primary retrieval, 1s for slow external APIs depending on SLA). The playbook includes a prescriptive fallback ladder (cached result -> short-summary -> safe-decline).

Related work: ENG-2124 (adaptive routing prototype), DOC-87 (docs backlog item for tooling quickstarts). This complements ongoing RAG session replay and structured-output examples.

Why unique: There are many RAG quickstarts; this one focuses specifically on runtime guardrails for tool execution and provides tiny runnable adapters to make the pattern adoptable without a heavy infra lift.
